MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY MARCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #3
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ornamental Fish culture? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ornamental Fish culture.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ornamental Fish culture.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ornamental Fish culture.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Ornamental Fish culture.

2. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Burning crop residue every week

3. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Nitrogen gas only

4. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water always increases oxygen

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Record keeping in aquaculture? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Record keeping in aquaculture.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Record keeping in aquaculture.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Record keeping in aquaculture.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Record keeping in aquaculture.

6. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

7. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 37 °C

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish feeds and feeding? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish feeds and feeding.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Fish feeds and feeding.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish feeds and feeding.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish feeds and feeding.

9. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Producers
   D. Primary consumers only

10. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Milk souring
   D. Iron rusting

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Fish Ecology and Ecosystems and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Ornamental Fish culture and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Fish feeds and feeding and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Record keeping in aquaculture and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ornamental Fish culture.

2. C — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

3. B — Glucose and oxygen

4. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

5. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Record keeping in aquaculture.

6. D — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

7. C — 100 °C

8. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish feeds and feeding.

9. C — Producers

10. A — Ice melting to water

11. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.

12. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Fish Ecology and Ecosystems; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Ornamental Fish culture; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Fish feeds and feeding; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Record keeping in aquaculture; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
